mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q01.stem: Fixing one button of a two-hand control can allow the machine to operate while the freed hand is inside the danger area.
reasons: Fixing one button removes the requirement to keep both hands at the controls, creating crushing and other hazards.
This statement is true. Fixing one button removes the requirement to keep both hands at the controls, creating crushing and other hazards.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q02.stem: Drawing hatching consists of lines used only to show the travel range of moving parts.
reasons: This statement is false. Hatching indicates specific areas such as section cuts. Phantom lines may indicate movement ranges.
Hatching indicates specific areas such as section cuts. Phantom lines may indicate movement ranges.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q03.stem: An ammeter symbol in a circuit diagram directly shows the physical positions of its real terminals.
reasons: This statement is false. A functional symbol differs from actual shape and terminal layout; check terminal diagrams and specifications.
A functional symbol differs from actual shape and terminal layout; check terminal diagrams and specifications.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q04.stem: Even at the same length and cross-section, conductor resistance may change with material or temperature.
reasons: The resistivity ρ in R=ρℓ/S depends on material and temperature.
This statement is true. The resistivity ρ in R=ρℓ/S depends on material and temperature.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q05.stem: Even infrequent defects leading to electric shock require severity assessment and action.
reasons: Assess frequency and severity separately.
This statement is true. Assess frequency and severity separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q06.stem: All good electrical conductors necessarily have identical magnetic properties.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish conductivity from magnetism.
Distinguish conductivity from magnetism.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q07.stem: The parallel equivalent of two positive resistances is smaller than the smaller resistance.
reasons: Parallel connection adds current paths.
This statement is true. Parallel connection adds current paths.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q08.stem: OR outputs one only when exactly one input is one; for 11 it always outputs zero.
reasons: This statement is false. OR is satisfied when at least one input is one.
OR is satisfied when at least one input is one.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q09.stem: BJTs with the same external shape have a fixed B/C/E order across all manufacturers.
reasons: This statement is false. Shape alone does not establish terminal order.
Shape alone does not establish terminal order.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q10.stem: The film protecting a wiring pattern differs in role from the unwanted copper to remove.
reasons: Retain required copper and remove unwanted copper.
This statement is true. Retain required copper and remove unwanted copper.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q11.stem: At the same marked voltage, all DC and AC motor connections are interchangeable.
reasons: This statement is false. Several ratings and operating types must be checked.
Several ratings and operating types must be checked.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q12.stem: Flow control mainly relates to hydraulic-actuator speed.
reasons: Inspect speed, force and direction separately.
This statement is true. Inspect speed, force and direction separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q13.stem: If flat washers are missing, state the part number and shortage quantity when asking for verification.
reasons: Fastener configuration and torque are separate specifications.
This statement is true. Fastener configuration and torque are separate specifications.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q14.stem: An illuminance-meter reading always also determines magnetic flux density at the same value.
reasons: This statement is false. Light and magnetic field are different quantities.
Light and magnetic field are different quantities.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q15.stem: Apply theory and practical percentage thresholds independently to their respective sections.
reasons: Do not combine the sections into one total-based judgment.
This statement is true. Do not combine the sections into one total-based judgment.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q16.stem: Safety glasses and safety footwear address different hazards.
reasons: Choose PPE for the body area and hazard.
This statement is true. Choose PPE for the body area and hazard.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q17.stem: Implementing one measure absolutely eliminates every fault and human error.
reasons: This statement is false. A measure does not guarantee zero risk.
A measure does not guarantee zero risk.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q18.stem: Before collecting data with a check sheet, define the items and counting rules.
reasons: Collect comparable data.
This statement is true. Collect comparable data.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q19.stem: In an electron-transfer description, oxidation is a change in which a substance loses electrons.
reasons: The electron-accepting side undergoes reduction.
This statement is true. The electron-accepting side undergoes reduction.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q20.stem: Similar initial letters in standard numbers establish identical revisions and requirements.
reasons: This statement is false. The complete number, revision and scope are needed.
The complete number, revision and scope are needed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q21.stem: Hard and annealed copper differ only in name; processing condition and every property are identical.
reasons: This statement is false. Annealing and other treatment change the material condition.
Annealing and other treatment change the material condition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q22.stem: A quartz resonator uses properties such as stable vibration.
reasons: It concerns signal oscillation characteristics.
This statement is true. It concerns signal oscillation characteristics.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q23.stem: DC circuits have no transient states, so capacitors are never used in them.
reasons: This statement is false. DC circuits also involve time changes and energy-storing components.
DC circuits also involve time changes and energy-storing components.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q24.stem: Every resistance-scale spacing is equal, and multipliers must never be applied.
reasons: This statement is false. Read the appropriate scale and multiplier.
Read the appropriate scale and multiplier.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q25.stem: An electromagnetic relay uses coil magnetism to move contacts.
reasons: Compare coil and contact ratings.
This statement is true. Compare coil and contact ratings.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q26.stem: If a textbook says a method is seldom used now, existing examples need not be identified.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not turn an overview into a guarantee that no equipment of that type exists.
Do not turn an overview into a guarantee that no equipment of that type exists.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q27.stem: Sprues, runners and gates are different parts of the resin path into the product cavity.
reasons: Distinguish the inlet from ejection components.
This statement is true. Distinguish the inlet from ejection components.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q28.stem: Oscilloscope bandwidth and sample rate are different performance specifications.
reasons: Check multiple performance conditions.
This statement is true. Check multiple performance conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q29.stem: All products called biodegradable immediately disappear harmlessly wherever discarded.
reasons: This statement is false. Material names alone do not determine disposal.
Material names alone do not determine disposal.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q30.stem: Every aqueous solution always has pH only from 0 to 14, regardless of temperature and concentration.
reasons: This statement is false. The textbook’s basic range has assumptions for applicability.
The textbook’s basic range has assumptions for applicability.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q01.stem: A “No entry” sign marks an area where you want to retrieve a tool. What should you do?
options: Ignore meaning and consider only its color.
Remove the sign because the tool is needed.
Enter if it is only briefly.
Do not enter without authorization; verify the area and permission procedure.
reasons: Understand and observe meaning and scope as well as color.
Needing a tool does not authorize removing the sign.
Brief entry does not permit unauthorized access.
Read prohibition signs with their area and scope; work convenience does not create exceptions.
This counts the leading eight but omits the two position.
The four position is zero, so the sum is not eight plus four.
Weights are 8, 4, 2 and 1: 8+0+2+0=10.
This reads the digits as a decimal string without binary positional weights.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q03.stem: A designated box contains 37 parts against a requirement of 52. Another warehouse has not been checked. Which report is accurate?
options: The shortage is definitely the responsible person’s mistake.
The designated box is 15 short; the other warehouse remains unverified.
The entire company is definitely 15 short.
reasons: The shortage is verified, but its cause and anyone’s fault are not.
52−37=15 applies to the checked box. Do not report unverified stock or causes as facts.
Only the designated box has been checked, not company-wide stock.
Recording 15 unavailable parts creates a mismatch between actual stock and records.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q04.stem: Corresponding JIS and IEC numbers were found, but their edition years differ. What should be verified?
options: Assume all conditions match because the numbers correspond.
Compare editions, differences and contractual applicability.
Automatically treat the old edition as the latest.
reasons: Destination requirements are part of applicability checks.
Number correspondence does not guarantee identical editions or national differences.
Correspondence may still involve differences and editions; compare the product and requirements.
An older edition cannot automatically be treated as current.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q05.stem: A recovered box is checked for suitability and repeatedly used. What is this primarily?
reasons: Using a product again as it is is reuse; distinguish returning it to material resources through recycling.
The box is reused, not disposed of.
The box remains in its original form rather than being returned to material resources.
Its direct classification is reuse, not merely reducing consumption.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q06.stem: After implementing an improvement, which activity is PDCA Check?
options: Finish explaining without looking at actual items.
Declare the first idea to be the established cause.
Check effects with data using the same definitions and conditions.
reasons: Without actual items or evidence of results, effectiveness cannot be assessed.
Changing standards before verification skips evaluation in Check.
Declaring an initial idea to be a cause is not checking post-implementation effects.
Check evaluates results after implementation and connects evaluation to further improvement or standardization.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q07.stem: In the negative-resist concept, what remains after exposure and development?
options: Only copper after removing all resist.
reasons: Development removes unhardened regions in this negative-resist example.
Exposed hardened film remains, and development removes unhardened film. Do not generalize to every resist process.
Development selectively removes film rather than retaining it all.
Hardened film protecting required copper remains at development; this is not complete stripping.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q08.stem: For binary inputs A=1 and B=0, what is two-input AND output?
reasons: AND outputs one only when both inputs are one; B is zero.
AND output depends on inputs, rather than always being one.
AND requires every input to be one. With B=0, the output is zero.
Binary output is zero or one, not an arithmetic total of two.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q09.stem: Which tools create an internal thread in a hole in a plate?
options: A suitable pilot drill and tap.
Only a center punch and reamer.
A suitable pilot drill and die.
reasons: Drill the correct pilot diameter, then tap the internal thread. A die makes external threads.
Marking and finishing a hole do not form internal thread ridges.
Drilling a pilot hole does not yet produce thread ridges.
A pilot hole is needed, but dies are for external threads; taps create internal threads.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q10.stem: Which PCB step removes unwanted copper while retaining conductor patterns?
reasons: Exposure patterns photosensitive film rather than removing copper.
Assembly joins components; it does not remove unwanted PCB copper.
Applying protective film alone does not remove copper.
Subtractive etching removes unprotected unwanted copper, unlike component assembly.
